details: Self-directed learning permits adaptive choice of the next instance.
proof: A self-directed learner can emulate any learner and favorable presentation sequence used for $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{best}}$ by choosing the same next instance itself.  It may additionally adapt that choice to earlier feedback.  Thus $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{sd}}(\mathcal H)\le\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{best}}(\mathcal H)$.
name: Best Mistakes / Self-Directed Queries Complexity
